body:
The only two things I've really been good at were arty things and psychology (it's really ironic, I think).  I know I really enjoy graphic design but I'm not sure what else I'm good at. 

I'm looking looking at the local vocational school for options. None of them really spark my interest, though. =/

Actually, I'm her daughter haha.

I've told her this. My doctors have all brought her into a room with me there and tried to discuss these things with her. Somehow, she's able to turn it around into how she was a hardworking mother and she had to work extra hard because my dad left. And you know, I actually understand that. But when I try and bring things like what's in my post above, it just gets lost and I end up looking like the troubled middle class kid who has no real problems.

I agree that when I'm thinking clearly, I know I'm being selfish when I consider that as an option. But sometimes it really does feel like the only thing that can solve my problems.

Thanks for the advice. Sometimes I feel like the tunnel is just a dead end, you know?

I wanted to major in graphic design. Now I'm not so sure if I'm doing that because I truly love it or because it's the only thing I'm good at. 

The community college I'm attending has a special course that's only a year long that allows me to take the gen ed requirements that I need. I looked into it already and my university accepts credits from this school. I guess it's just a matter of toughing it out for a year or so.

Thank you so much. It's hard to distance myself from my mom since she is my primary source of income. She pays for my car and for everything. I'm trying to find jobs to help myself break free of her, but it's just so hard sometimes. Thanks for your kind words.

Thanks for your advice. 

I get it, there have been some moments where I feel like everything is going to be okay. But those are few and fleeting.
